title: Father's work for the Morrow family and their support for his music
summary: His father was a gardener for Dwight Morrow's family; the Morrows helped finance his music study in Boston.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: What kind of occupation was your family involved in?

Well, my dad was a sort of a caretaker, gardener and what have you. He worked for -- he used to cut grass and garden -- garden for the folks up on the hill, you know. That was his job. One person that he worked for in gardening and what have you was Dwight Morrow. You probably heard of the Morrow family from Englewood. And their daughter was Anne Morrow. She married Charles Lindbergh. And that was quite a gig there working for them, because it was a way of living, you know, means of living, and we got along very well.
What did he think about them? Did he ever talk to you about the family?

Yes. They were wonderful people. They did wonderful things for us. You know -- they -- for my family they were very wonderful. Of course, I didn't see too much of them because they were more or less travelers and big timers, you might say, in politics and all that.
When you say they did wonderful things for the family, like what?
Well, speaking of us, you mean?
They were very interested in my music.

And somehow they -- they had a lot to do with my financing my career in music later on. As a matter of fact, I'm sure that they were a big help to my family in sending me to music school in Boston -- in Boston when I got out of high school. I'm sure that they were a big help in my music, you know, the financial part.
They sent me away to Boston to study the bass. That's when I forgot all the little -- forgot about the little violin. I used to call it the squeak box.
I didn't like it too much, you know.
And I was so interested in the bass fiddle. So that it wound up that my folks sent me up to Boston to try to make a career in music, especially playing the bass fiddle.
